scope.statement: This review inspects the one preserved native-controls01 bootstrap/parent/worker stop and runs only tiny Python child and local-import cleanup probes. It does not authorize retry, controls, analyzer, JVM, admission, qualification, Git, or publication work.

bootstrap.terminal_error: FrozenBridge19Error: graph import added a non-stdlib process-global sys.modules entry at native_qualifier.py:315 during bootstrap context exit

child_started.interpretation: This receipt records the argv and environment passed by supervise; it is not a worker-owned observation of sys.orig_argv or os.environ.

worker_owned_preflight_receipt.reason: The worker raises at the argv assertion before its existing environment check and before any worker-owned receipt is written.

findings.finding: The worker's exact command receipt is correct, but the raw sys.orig_argv comparison is not portable to the bound macOS interpreter invocation. The parent records argv[0] as /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13. A tiny detached Python 3.13 child launched with that same interpreter path observes sys.orig_argv[0] as the resolved Cellar executable, while sys.executable is /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.13/bin/python3.13. The worker therefore fails at native_qualifier.py:581-584 before the ready phase even though the parent-generated worker argv and all request/review/FD/token/parent identity arguments match.

source_evidence.worker_command_generation: native_qualifier.py:430-431 command() returns PYTHON, -B, -E, the resolved wrapper path, and the worker request/review/FD/token/parent identity arguments
source_evidence.worker_assertion: native_qualifier.py:579-584 reads parent-started.json and requires started['argv'] == sys.orig_argv
source_evidence.child_receipt_generation: native_qualifier.py:500-506 writes child-started.json from the argv list passed by supervise, before the worker can report its own sys.orig_argv

receipt_evidence.worker_failure: ValueError: worker invocation differs from actual parent command receipt

tiny_probe.boundary: The probe uses a tiny child script and substitutes only that script's path at argv[2]; it does not import native qualifier code or invoke any runtime, JVM, analyzer, or control.

findings.required_repair: Make interpreter identity deterministic without weakening exact argument checks: either generate the child argv with the canonical executable identity observed by Python or compare argv[0] through an explicitly recorded canonicalization while retaining raw argv[0], exact argv[1:] and wrapper/request/review/FD/token/parent birth fields. Add a worker-owned immutable preflight receipt that records raw sys.orig_argv, sys.executable, the canonical interpreter identity, actual os.environ (or a bound digest plus exact expected fields), request/review/token and parent PID/birth before ready. Keep parent-generated and worker-observed receipts distinct; do not treat the current child-started receipt as worker observation.

findings.finding: The graph boundary guard correctly rejects a non-stdlib process-global module, but the native wrapper leaves its own dynamically loaded helper/process modules in sys.modules after the graph context snapshots the baseline. modules() calls close_on_error() before removing even its host modules, and load() never unregisters a successful random module name. Bootstrap therefore masks its normal return at native_qualifier.py:642/760, and parent teardown masks the original child ValueError at native_qualifier.py:714/745. This is a cleanup-order/ownership defect, not a reason to relax the graph boundary guard.

source_evidence.dynamic_loader: native_qualifier.py:78-92 inserts a random module name in sys.modules and leaves it registered on successful load
source_evidence.graph_snapshot: bifrost-v0140-frozen-bridge-19.py:462-466 snapshots process-global sys.modules before graph execution
post_snapshot_loads: native_qualifier.py:643 bootstrap loads _bootstrap_resources and :649 loads the retained process helper
source_evidence.teardown: native_qualifier.py:302-317 calls graph.import_context.close_on_error() at :315 before popping only hosts at :316-317
source_evidence.guard: bifrost-v0140-frozen-bridge-19.py:863-876 rejects every added non-stdlib sys.modules key; :954-959 close_on_error performs the check before clearing local graph bindings

receipt_evidence.bootstrap_trace: FrozenBridge19Error: graph import added a non-stdlib process-global sys.modules entry
receipt_evidence.parent_trace: ValueError: native control parent failed; inspect preserved receipts, followed by FrozenBridge19Error from modules().__exit__

result.observed_exception: BoundaryError: graph import added a non-stdlib process-global sys.modules entry

findings.required_repair: Add an explicit owned module scope for every successful load performed after graph construction. Remove only those exact owned names/objects before graph.import_context.close_on_error(), then close the graph and host scope in deterministic order. Preserve the boundary check and reject unowned/foreign non-stdlib additions. Cleanup errors must be recorded separately; when an operation already has an original exception, cleanup must not replace it or erase the preserved failure receipt.

argv_and_environment: Tiny Popen child launched through the bound /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13 path proves the observed interpreter identity and accepts only the canonicalized argv[0] representation; exact argv[1:] and wrapper/request/review/FD/token/parent-birth arguments remain required.

Positive and near-miss parent/worker receipt tests distinguish parent-generated argv/env from worker-observed sys.orig_argv/os.environ, including a changed interpreter path, changed flag, changed request hash, changed FD, changed token, changed parent birth, and a one-field environment difference.
The pre-ready mismatch remains a failed startup with no ready frame, no controls-started frame, no capture, no retry, and owned-child cleanup.
graph_cleanup: Tiny local module loaded after graph baseline is removed by owned identity before close_on_error and permits a normal return.
An unowned non-stdlib sys.modules addition remains a hard boundary failure; no broad sys.modules deletion or foreign-module allowance is accepted.
Normal return and an original body exception both retain their original semantics when cleanup succeeds or fails; cleanup failure is separately recorded and cannot mask the original error.

Bootstrap Popen failure, peer/worker exit, and post-Popen identity failure continue to preserve immutable receipts and owned-only cleanup under the existing 120-second handshake and 600/900/240-second bounds.
execution_boundaries: Do not add a retry, extra analyzer, JVM, engine, replay, admission, qualification, or publication action while repairing these startup defects.
Preserve exact birth identities, common flock ownership, anonymous pipe token gate, finite startup limits, ledger immutability and automatic_retry=false.

disposition.attempt_consumption: No native control result or qualification is inferred. Preserve this one started-and-failed invocation and do not retry under this review.
disposition.next_gate: Writer may prepare an append-only source repair and focused tiny-child/cleanup regressions. A new independent source review and a fresh exact invocation review are required before any later control invocation.

method: Read-only receipt/hash inspection plus two private /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13 -B -E tiny probes. No engine, JVM, analyzer, native control, runtime graph import, admission, qualification, replay, Git mutation, source edit, retry, or publication action was performed.
